answer: On $35,000 over 60 months at the May 2026 bank rate (7.14%) the payment is $695.36; a full point lower would cut it by only $16.43. In 76 one-year waits from August 2006 to May 2025 (bank rate now vs a year later, car price moved with the new-vehicle price index), waiting lowered the payment in 38.2% of cases; the median wait raised it by $1.17 a month. The rate fell in 50 of the 76 years, but the payment fell in only 52% of those, because prices rose (median +0.54%) and the largest one-year rate drop was 1.08 points. The best wait saved $27.82 a month. History, not a forecast.
guess: Shoppers waiting for rate cuts expect a lower rate to bring a noticeably lower payment and assume waiting a year pays off at least half the time.
changesDecision: A rate cut of the size seen in a year is worth tens of dollars a month at most on $35,000, and car price changes often cancelled it: waiting lowered the payment in fewer than four of ten past years. A shopper can weigh that small, uncertain gain against the costs of keeping the old car another year.

assumptions: Loan $35,000 now, 60 months, level payments, no down payment change, fees or trade-in.
The car price a year later moves with the new-vehicle consumer price index (quality-adjusted), not sticker prices or incentives.
Bank survey rates stand for the rate the shopper would get; dealer, captive and credit-union rates are not modeled.
Costs of keeping the old car (repairs, fuel) are not counted.
limits: History, not a forecast. Quarterly bank survey since 2006 only; the price index adjusts for quality, so transaction prices may have risen faster than shown. Individual rates depend on credit and lender. Does not model promotional dealer rates.
